parsed.explanation: Combined regime for a visiting trans adult or family. No trans-specific criminal offence is documented, and sexual-orientation hate-crime doubling and a 1988 decriminalisation are present, though gender-identity coverage of these is unresolved. The main exposure is border and custody: the main airport has no trans-specific procedure, and a 2023 account documents surgery being demanded for gender recognition and humiliating detention. Trans prisoners are documented as isolated by default, with men's-prison holding at times and no statute or regulation on placement. Violence is documented as rising in 2025 with dating-app traps and organised ambushes, but no denominator exists. Mitigators are working courts, a 2023 search regulation, and a 2025 dead-name removal law. Rated in the Elevated band.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented: 2023 airport account of gender-identity screening where security insisted surgery was required for gender recognition; humiliating questioning and detention. Mismatched documents can out a visitor at the border.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented for visitors. Resident legal gender change without surgery (2015 policy) does not clearly reach foreign-issued documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign passport mismatch leads to secondary questioning, which can escalate to detention and custody placement (see custody factor).

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: isolation/segregation is the default management of trans prisoners; trans women have at times been held in men's prisons; 2019 relief was case-specific and later outcome unreported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Documented: 2023 police search regulation after complaints of humiliating searches of trans detainees; courts have ordered transfer and hormone therapy in one case.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border detention can route a visitor into this custody regime; whether case-by-case relief extends to a foreign detainee is not established.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Documented: national prison service applies isolation-based custody; no statute or regulation on placement by gender identity.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Not documented as a national placement rule. Court-ordered relief has happened in individual cases only.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Single national system; no subnational variation documented for custody or airport.

care_services.exposure: Documented: transition care is gated by a single hospital committee; many trans residents report approval trouble and pay out of pocket. Visitor access to that committee is not documented.
care_services.protection: Documented: public insurance can cover treatment after committee approval; 2022 directive bars licensed professionals from conversion therapy.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing ongoing hormones faces gatekeeping that is not documented as open to foreigners.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: airport screening treats trans identity as a document problem requiring surgery; a foreign head of state's rhetoric is reported as raising local fear.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Documented: courts have overturned a Pride ban and blocked a fast-track gender-change reversal (2025).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing at the border is the main channel for outing to security staff.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for minors. The dossier shows no minor-specific border or custody rule; an adult guardian's documents would face the same screening.
minors_guardians.interaction: A trans adult travelling with a child could face border questioning that involves the child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented: 433 homophobic/transphobic physical incidents in 2025, with dating-app traps and organised ambushes; lethal attacks at pride events in 2005, 2009 and 2015. No denominator, so per-capita risk cannot be set.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Documented: double punishment for sexual-orientation-motivated violence; court overturned a municipal Pride ban; public outcry and a square renamed after the 2015 victim.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Organised lures target visitors and locals alike; police response to ambushes is not documented in detail.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Gender-identity coverage of the 1992–2000 anti-discrimination and hate-crime statutes is unresolved. Conflicting claims on legal gender recognition and LGBTI registration are unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Documented: working courts on several occasions; 2024 identity-card name removal; 2025 high court ruling upholding a certificate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse is documented mainly for residents; no record of relief for a detained foreign visitor.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.35-A's universal visitor registry with refusal and no remedy. This dossier documents no entry-ban or universal refusal regime, only discretionary screening with humiliation and detention.

Similar. Both involve discretionary secondary screening, humiliating questioning and partial exposure with no criminal charge at entry. This dossier adds documented isolation custody and organised violence, but also a 2023 search regulation and working courts.

Lower than 0.75-C, which has documented border training, written reasons and compensation for unlawful holding. This dossier documents no visitor-specific border training and a surgery-demanding screening incident.

parsed.synthesis: The dominant traveller-facing exposure is the border: mismatched documents can trigger humiliating questioning and detention with no visitor procedure, and surgery has been demanded for gender recognition. If detained, custody defaults to isolation, with men's-prison holding documented at times and relief only case by case. Violence is elevated, with organised ambushes and lethal pride attacks, but no denominator exists. Courts, hate-crime doubling and a 2023 search regulation are real mitigators, but they reach residents more than visitors. The combined regime sits in the Elevated band.
